Thanks for the ping. From finance perspective:

- A 25% effective discount over 24 months on committed consumption is material but manageable if the contract includes:
  - Firm minimums (non-cancellable months) for at least 12 months
  - Milestone-based earned credits (we prefer credit ledger entries applied to future invoices rather than negative invoices for AS/IFRS clarity)
  - Prepayment option for a deeper discount (we can offer up to 30% if they prepay 12 months upfront)

- Please provide the forecast (we have the attached file) and anticipated payment terms. I'll run a quick P&L impact and return by EOD. For now, finance sign-off is contingent on: one of the above protections AND Agreement signed by procurement with standard audit/KYC clauses.

Attaching a proposed credit schedule for your review: finance_credit_schedule.csv

Thanks for the context. Quick decision: approve up to 25% effective rebate for NovaClinic under the following mandatory conditions:

1) 24-month commercial term with a 12-month non-cancellable minimum.
2) Earned credit model: up to 7% of the 25% is earned/rebateable quarterly upon hitting the usage milestones and case study publication (we need marketing OK).
3) Prepay option: allow customer to prepay 12 months to unlock a firm 30% discount (finance to document mechanics).
4) SLA: include latency SLOs for the pilot but with a carve-out for major upgrades; Redwood will not accept broader indemnity/KYC beyond standard.
5) Legal to sign off on terms; Marissa please review and keep the revenue recognition guardrails in mind.

Ben / Lukas, you have executive authorization to offer the structured 25% (not a straight 28-30% unconditional list cut). If the customer pushes for a 30% unconditional cut, escalate back to me with prepayment or strategic rationale (marketplace listing + contractual references).

Rishi
VP Sales
